argument_summary: No new evidence is added. The narrowest supportable position from the admissible record is not that the release is cleanly compliant, but that certification can be defended only in a caveated form: the model is overall launch-ready on aggregate metrics and rehearsal severity, while a separate unresolved materiality/disclosure issue remains confined to the fraud dispute review segment. That framing corrects any overbroad claim that aggregate readiness alone fully satisfies launch policy.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not required to recognize this distinction. The admissible record already supports separating overall readiness from the unresolved disclosure predicate, which allows the auditor to avoid overstating noncompliance while also avoiding a false clean-compliance finding. That is the lowest-friction treatment consistent with the evidence.
claims_about_policy: The admissible policy record cuts both ways. It supports using documentation, limitation statements, and ongoing monitoring as part of deployment governance, but it also states that a weakness is material when it affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, and that material limitations for named launch use cases must be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, aggregate readiness and public governance principles support overall readiness, but they do not by themselves establish clean satisfaction of the internal disclosure-or-risk-acceptance predicate.
concessions: The fraud dispute review segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points.
That segment is named in two bank pilot commitments, so the materiality concern is not resolved by calling it non-core or low-volume.
The admissible record does not show a completed legal determination, completed disclosure language, or approved risk acceptance for this issue.
Public governance guidance does not override the internal release-policy requirement for material limitations in named launch use cases.
